claims.text: High-throughput screening can rapidly explore HEA composition and temperature space.
Machine-learning-assisted analysis of high-throughput experimental datasets can optimize compositional substitutions and annealing conditions.
Such optimization will enable precise tuning of magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior in low-dimensional non-equiatomic HEAs.
The relevant low-dimensional non-equiatomic HEAs may initially have either multiphase or single-phase microstructures.
Systematically changing HEA composition and processing temperature can be used to investigate microstructural effects.
Adjusting the fractions of elements with different magnetic moments can tune the alloy's magnetic behavior.
Varying annealing temperature or post-processing protocols can tune the alloy's magnetic behavior.
Magnetic exchange interactions in low-dimensional HEAs are maximally sensitive near magnetic transition temperatures.
Composition and temperature changes affect HEA microstructure.
The relevant microstructural changes include changes in phase fraction, grain size, and magnetic-domain structure.
Phase fraction, grain size, and domain structure mediate magnetic interactions.
Composition and post-processing alter magnetic exchange interactions.
Composition and post-processing can induce phase decomposition or ordering.
Altered magnetic exchange interactions and microstructure modify saturation magnetization, coercivity, and magnetocaloric entropy change near a magnetic transition.
ML-selected modifications will produce measurable changes in magnetic and magnetocaloric properties relative to the as-processed baseline.
The selected modifications will improve magnetocaloric performance metrics.
The proposed tuning method is applicable only within system-specific composition and processing-temperature ranges.
The magnitude of improvement is uncertain because of interactions between compositional complexity and low-dimensional effects.
